findings.title: Rendering relationship-selected XML can bypass depth limits and exhaust the process stack
findings.summary: A document author can give an auxiliary XML part a non-.xml filename and reference it as styles. Admission skips its XML policy, then PDF/PNG rendering parses that part with unbounded recursive descent, allowing process termination through stack exhaustion.

severity.rationale: An attacker-supplied document can cause deterministic unbounded recursion during an ordinary public conversion. Impact is availability of the processing process; service-wide exposure depends on caller deployment and process isolation.
severity.changeConditions: Effective per-document worker isolation limits impact; enforcing active XML policy on every consumed XML part removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Static source trace establishes suffix-only admission, unconstrained internal styles target selection, and unchecked recursive parsing. Runtime stack size and exact failure depth were not measured.

codeEvidence.label: Admission selects XML policy by suffix
codeEvidence.explanation: Only .xml/.rels entries receive XML policy; other parts are drained and counted.

codeEvidence.label: Only the main part receives an extension-independent check
codeEvidence.explanation: The extra depth check covers main_part only, leaving relationship-selected auxiliary XML outside policy.

codeEvidence.label: Public conversion admits then opens package
codeEvidence.explanation: with_layout admits bytes before opening PartFs; downstream auxiliary XML comes from the same attacker package.

codeEvidence.label: Styles relationships select arbitrary internal parts
codeEvidence.explanation: No extension constraint is applied to the styles target.

codeEvidence.label: Styles loader invokes permissive DOM parser
codeEvidence.explanation: The chosen part is parsed by parse_xdocument without checked validation.

codeEvidence.label: Recursive descent has no depth guard
codeEvidence.explanation: Each child element recurses directly, allowing a deeply nested auxiliary part to exhaust stack.

rootCause.summary: Admission applies XML depth/tag budgets based on filename suffix and adds an exception only for the main part. main_rel_part resolves a document-controlled styles relationship regardless of extension; load_stylesheet passes its content to the permissive DOM parser, whose parse_element recursively descends without a depth limit. PartFs and Strict normalization enforce byte budgets but never add XML validation to that auxiliary part.

findings.remediation: Validate every part as XML immediately before a semantic XML consumer parses it, using the active InputLimits regardless of suffix; use checked parsers or make admission classify all XML parts through content types and relationships.

counterEvidence: Admission bounds compressed/inflated bytes and XML depth for .xml/.rels; a nonstandard main part is also explicitly checked.
The unchecked raw XML API is documented trusted-only; the flaw is its automatic use after incomplete package admission, rather than that public low-level API by itself.
SECURITY.md recommends per-process CPU/memory limits, which can contain but do not prevent process stack exhaustion.
limitations: No crafted document or runtime reproduction executed.
Confirmed styles route; sibling relationship-selected parser routes remain under review.
validation.summary: The parent verified that a normal main document and .rels can select a deeply nested auxiliary styles part under a non-XML suffix. Neither PartFs::open nor strict_to_transitional_docx adds depth policy to it before load_stylesheet calls parse_xdocument; no requirement for styles suffix or content-type blocks this route.

dataflow.summary: DOCX styles relationship and styles.bin -> suffix-only admission -> bounded PartFs load -> main_rel_part(styles) -> load_stylesheet -> parse_xdocument -> recursive parse_element -> stack exhaustion

impact.why: Processing process can terminate; availability of other work depends on embedding.

likelihood.why: Part naming and relationship values are document-controlled; no special option is needed.

limitations: No code execution, data theft or remote deployment is established.

reachability.summary: Public conversion with default settings is sufficient; the attacker controls document bytes and needs no local file, shell or privileged account access. CLI/Python/WASM callers expose the same core converter when enabled.
reachability.attacker: Author of an untrusted document processed by a victim
preconditions: Victim processes attacker-controlled DOCX through the converter.

attackPath.summary: Submit a DOCX with a valid main document whose styles relationship selects a deeply nested styles.bin, then invoke public PDF/PNG rendering.

remediationTests: A styles relationship to deeply nested styles.bin must return INVALID_XML under default limits.
Repeat for settings, theme, numbering, headers/footers, notes, and other relationship-selected XML consumers, including renamed main parts.
preventiveControls: Centralize checked package XML access so consumers cannot silently bypass active policy.

findings.title: Rendering an HTML chunk can allocate gigabytes from a single colspan value
findings.summary: A document author can place a very large colspan in a small embedded HTML table. Ordinary DOCX rendering expands it into one grid XML element per column before any generated-size limit, exhausting CPU/memory despite package admission bounds.

severity.rationale: A tiny attacker-controlled document field causes highly amplified resource consumption in public conversion paths. Impact is processing availability; isolated workers reduce shared-service impact.
severity.changeConditions: A strict generated-output and column budget enforced before expansion removes this path; process limits contain its blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Both independent baseline and focused investigator identified the mechanism; parent verified input parsing, post-admission expansion and allocation loop statically. No runtime reproduction was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Rendering expands chunks after admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Victim conversion admits original bytes then expands attacker-controlled package HTML before DOM construction.

codeEvidence.label: Relationship-selected bytes become generated WML
codeEvidence.explanation: Document-controlled chunk id loads package bytes which chunk_html decodes and html_to_wml expands.

codeEvidence.label: HTML colspan has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: An HTML author controls an arbitrary usize span; minimum one is the only restriction.

codeEvidence.label: One grid XML element is emitted per declared column
codeEvidence.explanation: A tiny numeric field drives cols iterations and unbounded String growth before downstream layout or output checks.

rootCause.summary: with_layout expands document-selected altChunk bytes after original ZIP/XML admission. HTML Builder::start accepts a colspan up to usize::MAX, end_table sums spans and emits gridCol once per declared column. No maximum column count or generated-WML byte budget is passed into expand, so a short HTML table can demand gigabytes before parser/output safeguards can act.

findings.remediation: Reject excessive per-cell and aggregate column spans before generating XML, use checked arithmetic, and enforce a cumulative generated-WML byte/work budget inside altChunk expansion with a typed refusal.

counterEvidence: Original archive size, entry and inflation limits apply before expansion, preventing ZIP bombs but not semantic numeric amplification.
Native process resource limits can terminate/contain a worker, not make the conversion return a bounded refusal.
limitations: No application code or exploit input was executed; platform allocation failure details were not measured.
validation.summary: Parent verified that colspan=1000000000 fits both native and wasm32 usize, survives the minimum-one conversion and drives one billion String append iterations. The original HTML stays small and normal input admission does not inspect its numeric semantics or charge generated XML.

dataflow.summary: DOCX altChunk relationship -> package bytes -> chunk_html -> html_to_wml -> arbitrary usize cell span -> sum cols -> gridCol append loop -> memory/CPU exhaustion

impact.why: Worker or embedding application can be terminated or stalled by runaway generated XML.

likelihood.why: No special feature option or external resource is needed; a small valid HTML chunk suffices.

limitations: No file disclosure or code execution established.

reachability.summary: Default public PDF/PNG converter expands internal altChunk parts after admission. Attacker needs only control over a document processed by the victim.
preconditions: Victim invokes document rendering on the supplied file.

attackPath.summary: Have a victim render a DOCX whose main document includes an internal altChunk HTML table with a huge positive colspan.

remediationTests: A tiny HTML chunk with colspan=1000000000 must refuse before allocation.
Check multi-cell aggregate span overflow and repeated/nested table expansion budgets.
preventiveControls: Charge representation expansion to explicit output/work budgets rather than relying only on compressed/inflated input limits.

surfaces.label: Document XML admission and relationship-selected converter parts
surfaces.notes: Validated suffix-based admission bypass: src/admission.rs:532-569; src/convert/mod.rs:3480-3501,21310-21321; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:660-664. Byte budgets do not enforce auxiliary XML depth.

candidate.title: Non-XML suffix styles part bypasses admission XML depth enforcement
candidate.evidence: Admission scans XML only by .xml/.rels suffix (src/admission.rs:533-543), while converter follows arbitrary styles relationship targets (load_stylesheet, main_rel_part) into unchecked recursive Dom parser. A deeply nested styles.bin bypasses max_xml_depth and reaches recursive parse_element, likely process stack exhaustion.

surfaces.label: altChunk HTML table expansion
surfaces.notes: Validated unlimited colspan -> per-column XML expansion at src/convert/altchunk.rs:469-491,557-567; generated output grows after admission at src/convert/mod.rs:790-798.

x
triggers many-GB allocation during admitted DOCX -> PDF/PNG. Admission only bounds input ZIP/XML; generated WML expansion occurs after admission.

candidate.title: Unbounded OOXML gridSpan drives table vectors beyond admission budgets
candidate.evidence: raw OOXML w:gridSpan unrestricted usize in cell_span (src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215), read_table uses each colspan in occupancy and allocates cols=vec![each; occupancy] / resize at 13604-13615; later resolve_table_merges resizes open to col+span at 14637-14638. A tiny admitted DOCX table with one cell and gridSpan=1000000000 requests multi-GB vectors without altChunk.
candidate.additionalEvidence: Sibling w:gridBefore/w:gridAfter parse unrestricted usize at src/convert/mod.rs:14340-14346, become RawCell.colspan and share occupancy allocations.
